topic: How does the 14.6% bandwidth affect frequency planning for multi-satellite networks with adjacent channel interference risks?
consensus_response: The 14.6% bandwidth constraint severely impacts frequency planning in multi-satellite networks, increasing adjacent channel interference (ACI) risks due to reduced spectral separation between channels. This leads to decreased capacity and link margin. Combining Pilot-Assisted Channel Estimation (PACE) with Frequency Hopping (FH) and Non-Coherent Detection (NCD) can mitigate ACI by optimizing frequency reuse and improving detection accuracy. The hybrid approach enables more efficient frequency reuse, increasing capacity while reducing error rates.
reference_context: The reference context provides various studies on satellite communication systems, including the effects of frequency reuse, channel allocation, and interference mitigation. Notably, a study on downlink coverage and rate analysis for low-Earth orbit satellite constellations using stochastic geometry shows that increasing the number of orthogonal channels can improve data rate but also degrades it by making only a portion of the whole band available for each group of satellites.
